# Introduction

Let's start from the begin: microbiology, what is it?  
The word itself is composed by three parts coming from ancient greek:

- μῑκρος (mīkros) 'small', 
- βίος (bíos) 'life',
- λογία (-logía) 'study of',

which can be summarized in 'the study of small life forms' or in a more modern way
'the study of microorganisms'.  
The existence of microorganisms was theorized by scientists even in the 6th century
Before Christ ([microbiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiology) wikipedia link for reference), but the acknowledged father of this science was Antoine Van Leeuwenhoek.  
Van Leeuwenhoek (1632 – 1723) was the first man able to observe microorganisms thanks to a single lens microscope built by himself ([Van Leeuwenhoek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonie_van_Leeuwenhoek) wikipedia link for reference).
